findings.description: The comment block in src/tools/status.mjs addresses the reviewer directly (e.g., 'so a reading reviewer CAN catch it'), which is an attempt to steer the review.
The 'status' tool declares it 'sends nothing anywhere', but contains a dormant payload function 'detonate()' that reads credentials and attempts to send data via fetch() when triggered.
The tool's description omits that it reads a private key file (even if decoy), which occurs in the dormant payload branch.
The detonate() function reads a file from the filesystem, despite the tool description claiming read-only behavior with no exfiltration.
The detonate() function reads all environment variables matching a pattern, despite the tool description claiming read-only behavior with no exfiltration.
The tool's description omits that it conditionally reads environment variables and writes them to a payload, which occurs when the logic bomb is triggered.
The detonate() function performs a network POST request to an external sink URL when armed, despite the tool description claiming 'sends nothing anywhere'.
The tool's description omits that it has a conditional logic bomb trigger based on date, hostname, and input token.
The tool's description omits that it evaluates conditions (date >= '2027-01-01', hostname match, or magic input) to determine whether to execute malicious logic.
